claim.pdf_says: Headings printed on page 157 in the normal clause hierarchy: "8.4.3.1.4  General rules" (a fourth-level clause under 8.4.3.1), then "8.4.3.2  Function-identifier", "8.4.3.2.1  General", "8.4.3.2.2  General format", "8.4.3.2.3  Syntax rules".
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 6794-6828: "## **8.4.3.1.4 General rules**", "## **8.4.3.2 Function-identifier**", "### **8.4.3.2.1 General**", "### **8.4.3.2.2 General format**", "### **8.4.3.2.3 Syntax rules**" — heading text wrapped in bold markup, and none of the five carries the anchor that every neighbouring page in this run uses (e.g. page 161: "" + "#### 8.4.3.3.1 General").
claim.why_it_matters: Page 157 is the only page in this batch whose clause headings deviate from the document's own convention: the four-part clause 8.4.3.1.4 sits at markdown level 2, the same level as its uncle 8.4.3.2 (page 161 correctly puts 8.4.3.3.1 at level 4 under 8.4.3.3 at level 3), so a generated TOC shows 8.4.3.1.4 as a peer of 8.4.3.2; and the five missing section anchors mean citations of the form #section-8-4-3-2-2 (the Function-identifier general format, a figure this compiler cites) have no target.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. No heading is missing and no PDF content is absent from the transcription. (1) Text presence: the 300-dpi render of page 157 (printed page 127) prints exactly five clause headings — "8.4.3.1.4 General rules", "8.4.3.2 Function-identifier", "8.4.3.2.1 General", "8.4.3.2.2 General format", "8.4.3.2.3 Syntax rules" — and all five appear in specs/ISO_COBOL.md at lines 6794, 6812, 6814, 6818, 6828, inside the page-157 block (page markers at 6785 and 6837), with the clause numbers and titles verbatim correct. The claim's own markdown_says field concedes this, so the 'missing-heading' kind is a misnomer: nothing was dropped. (2) The heading-LEVEL charge rests on a false premise. The claim asserts page 157 is 'the only page in this batch whose clause headings deviate from the document's own convention.' It is not: the entire 8.4.3.1/8.4.3.2 run is flat at level 2 — 8.4.3 Identifiers, 8.4.3.1 Identifier, 8.4.3.1.1 General, 8.4.3.1.2 General format (pages 154-155), 8.4.3.1.3 Syntax rules (page 156) and 8.4.3.2.4 General rules (page 159, line 6891) are ALL '##'. The depth-encoding style the claim cites as canonical begins only at 8.4.3.3 on page 161 ('### 8.4.3.3' + '#### 8.4.3.3.1'). Page 157 therefore matches its four immediate neighbours; page 161 is where the style changes. Page 157 is the majority behaviour in this run, not an outlier. (3) The flat level also mirrors the print. In the rendered page the five headings are set in visually identical bold serif type at the same point size — the PDF does not distinguish clause depth typographically here at all. Hierarchy is carried solely by the dotted clause number, which the markdown preserves exactly, so a reader still sees 8.4.3.1.4 as subordinate to 8.4.3.1 and 8.4.3.2.2 as subordinate to 8.4.3.2. Nothing about the spec's meaning, syntax or rule structure changes. (4) The '**...**' wrapping is inert cosmetic markup on text a heading already renders bold; it is exactly the 'only formatting' class of difference this verification is instructed to reject. (5) The missing '' anchors are not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy at all: the PDF contains no HTML anchors, so nothing was lost from the source. Those anchors are transcription-side navigation metadata generated by the conversion tooling. Their absence is confirmed (anchors run section-8-4-3 through section-8-4-3-1-3 at lines 6658-6734, then jump to section-8-4-3-2-4 at 6890, skipping five), but it is an internal convenience gap, not a fidelity defect against the standard.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy — reject as a spec-reconciliation finding. All five page-157 clause headings are transcribed with correct numbers and titles; the differences are markup only (bold wrapping, '##' instead of '###'/'####'), and the claim's premise that page 157 uniquely breaks a document-wide convention is factually wrong, since pages 154, 155, 156 and 159 use the same flat '##' level and the deeper style starts at page 161. One narrower, corroborated but NON-PDF issue is worth filing separately as transcription hygiene rather than reconciliation: five '<a id="section-...">' anchors are absent (section-8-4-3-1-4, -2, -2-1, -2-2, -2-3), and as a consequence the table-of-contents row at line 245 renders as unlinked plain text — '8.4.3.2 Function-identifier ... 127' — while every neighbouring TOC row (8.4.3.1 at 244, 8.4.3.3 at 246) is a live link. That is a dead-link/navigation defect in the markdown's own apparatus, fixable by adding the anchors and re-linking line 245, and it should not be recorded as the PDF and the markdown disagreeing about what the standard says.
